answer: A bridge contract then escrows reputation earned over epochs, slashing the stake if duplicate keys appear. Sybil resistance can work like a guarded wharf: each new agent must stake a bond and pass a quill-signed proof-of-work challenge tied to a unique hardware key, so forging identities costs real compute and locked capital. Attackers must pay for every fake identity and risk losing deposits, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. This model fits agent once0004's threat model.
